answer_1.quote: we propose the new task of Schema-guided Natural Language Generation, where we take a turn-level schema as input and generate a natural language string describing the required content...
datasets: SG-NLG (repurposed DSTC8 Schema-Guided State Tracking dataset)
answer_1.outputs: delexicalized system prompts/templates (natural language strings with $slot placeholders)

answer_2.quote: We focus on three distinct metric types: similarity to references, semantic accuracy, and diversity... Similarity to references... we use BLEU... and METEOR... Semantic accuracy... we compute the slot error rate (SER)... Diversity... we measure distinct-N and novelty...

answer_4.quote: We conduct an annotation study to evaluate our schema-guided output quality. We randomly sample 50 MRs... collect 3 judgments per output for each model as well as a reference... ask the annotators to give a binary rating for each output across 3 dimensions: grammar, naturalness, and semantics... We also get an "overall" rating on a 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each generated output on grammar, naturalness, semantics (binary correctness) and provide an overall quality score on a 1‑5 Likert scale.
